messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — elevated 5xx rate observed for Hosted API (us-east-1) and Dedicated pools in us-east-1. Error signature: upstream IAM/STs errors + API Gateway 504/503s. Correlation: increased latency to sts.amazonaws.com. Pager created and paging @Sam (oncall)
Sam (oncall): I'm on pager, looking. First pass: Are we seeing token failures or our auth proxy?
Priya (SRE): Observability -> spike in calls to AWS STS from token-renewer service. Rate errors: `Throttling` and `403` in a short window. Dedicated pools show 503 gateway errors when auth fails during init.
Alex (runtime): Confirmed - model serving tasks trying to fetch credentials for new workers; if STS fails the request path returns 503 on our edge. Stack: API GW -> auth-proxy -> token-renewer -> STS.
Lisa (support): Support reporting multiple customers seeing generation errors and rests with 5xx. Two enterprise customers called in because Dedicated pools timed out.
Taylor (product): Need quick impact summary for CSMs. Which customers affected and degraded surfaces? embeddings and completion endpoints primarily?
Sam (oncall): Short note: completions and streaming endpoints most impacted due to new session creation. Long-lived sessions still OK. Rough estimate: 8% of hosted traffic, 12% of some Dedicated pools in us-east-1.
Priya (SRE): Root cause hypothesis: regional STS rate limiting / degraded control plane in us-east-1. AWS health dashboard shows elevated errors for IAM/STS in region. Link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ (checked)
infra-bot: Created incident channel and incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/2795554321 (auto)
Sam (oncall): Mitigation plan proposal: (1) throttle token-renewer fanout, (2) route new worker credential fetches through fallback region (eu-west-1) where possible, (3) enable short-circuit cached creds for Dedicated provisioner for 15m.
Alex (runtime): For Dedicated pools, we can flip `prefer-local-creds` -> false for new nodes so they try cached credentials path first. Patch is in `infra/credentials/patch-2026-03-15` — applying now.
Priya (SRE): Rolling change: add small sleep and jitter to token-renewer concurrency and double backoff on 429s. Patch command:
```bash
# temporary backoff change
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/token-renewer BACKOFF_BASE_MS=500 BACKOFF_MAX_MS=10000
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/token-renewer
```
Sam (oncall): Doing that. Restarting token-renewer — will monitor error rate.
(5m later)
Sam (oncall): token-renewer rollout complete, observed a drop in consecutive 429s but still elevated single-call failures.
Priya (SRE): Enabling cross-region STS fallback for provisioning flow. Note: this increases latency but avoids outright failures. Deploying config toggle `sts_fallback_region=eu-west-1` to environment for `provisioner`.
Alex (runtime): Patch applied to provisioner. Also adding a temporary route in edge router to prefer eu-west-1 for auth calls when us-east-1 returns STS errors. Command: `routerctl set-policy auth_region=eu-west-1 if region==us-east-1 and sts_error_count>10`
Sam (oncall): Edge policy applied. Observing a drop in 5xx and lower error percent in Hosted API. Dedicated pools still have a tail of timeouts — investigating node bootstrap logs.
Lisa (support): Notifying top affected customers: pinging CSMs with preliminary ticket: high-level - intermittent failures in us-east-1, mitigations applied, ETA monitoring.
Taylor (product): Make sure to flag any SLA hits for enterprise. Provide list of Dedicated customers in us-east-1 to account team.
Priya (SRE): Quick log snippet from token-renewer showing STS throttles:
```
[2026-03-15T04:12:33Z] WARN sts_call: Throttling - 429 - RequestId: abcdef-1234 - retrying
[2026-03-15T04:12:33Z] ERROR kube_init: failed to assume role for node-xx - AccessDenied/Throttling
[2026-03-15T04:12:35Z] INFO backoff: waiting 320ms before retry
```
Sam (oncall): Customer impact assessment (quick): Hosted API - increased token latency causing 5xx for new sessions -> approx 6-10% Uptime hit for those flows in us-east-1 over last 20m. Dedicated - some pools experienced failed node joins -> reduced capacity ~10% for affected pools.
Alex (runtime): To limit blast radius, temporarily disable autoscaling up for affected Dedicated pools (so we don't bootstrap new nodes that will fail and cause upstream errors). Command: `infractl pool set-autoscale pool-us-east-1-ml false`
Priya (SRE): Done. Also enabling alert mute for noisy 429 alerts until we prove recover.
(10m later)
Sam (oncall): Metric update: 5xx rate down from peak 18% to 3% in hosted; Dedicated pool join failure rate reduced. Still watching.
Lisa (support): Customers are seeing improvements. CSMs updated. One customer asked for post-incident root cause — will provide after RCA.
Alex (runtime): Plan for next 1hr: keep STS fallback enabled, keep token-renewer backoff, keep autoscale disabled for affected pools, monitor appliance.
Taylor (product): Communications plan: status page update - indicate degraded in us-east-1 with mitigations and ETA for monitoring. Draft will be posted by support in 5m.
Sam (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing pager to Priya for next shift — leaving runbook notes in the incident doc and current mitigation toggles. Priya, can you keep watch for 1h and escalate to runtime if nodes fail again?
Priya (SRE): Acknowledged handoff. Will keep monitoring and will escalate if error rate rises above 8% again.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV2. All mitigation toggles documented in incident doc.
infra-bot: Recorded actions: token-renewer backoff applied; sts_fallback_region set to eu-west-1; autoscale disabled for pool-us-east-1-ml.
(1h later)
Priya (SRE): Post-check - metrics back to baseline over 30m. STS errors largely resolved in us-east-1 per AWS. Rolling back temporary workarounds: re-enable autoscale for pools, remove sts_fallback_region toggle, revert prefer-local-creds change after 30m stable.
Alex (runtime): Reverted router policy and prefer-local-creds change.
Sam (oncall): Final check: 5xx baseline restored, no active alerts. Moving to resolved state but leaving doc open for RCA.
Taylor (product): Good. Please prepare a short customer-facing timeline and a tech RCA for internal review.
Lisa (support): Notified CSMs that services stabilized and we will send follow-up with timeline.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED (post-mitigation monitoring period passed). Please attach RCA and timeline to incident doc. :white_check_mark:
